content:
alex: heads-up: restore canary failing in staging, started ~11:03 UTC. error looks KMS/grant-related
ops-bot: incident created -> restore-canary-failures (pager duty) :rotating_light:
alex: paste of tail from restore worker:
```
2024-11-10T11:03:02Z ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException - InvalidGrant: grant has expired (grantId=gr-0abcd1234)
stack: ...
```
morgan: @alex can you grab the uploader/kms-proxy logs around that time (CreateGrant/GenerateDataKeyWithGrant)?
alex: on it. quick skim: kms-proxy issued CreateGrant at 2024-11-10T11:02:55Z, uploader called Decrypt at 2024-11-10T11:03:58Z and got InvalidGrant
priya: wait — that suggests grant was short-lived. what is GRANT_TTL set to?
lee: checking hosts: uploader-host-1 ntp shows when=7200 (last poll 2h ago). output:
```
$ ntpq -p
remote           refid      st t when poll reach   delay   offset  jitter
*time.cloudflare 10.0.0.1    2  7200 1024  377    12.345   0.512   0.23
```
lee: offset small but "when" stale => ntpd not running polls frequently
morgan: that would cause skew between kms-proxy and uploader. kms-proxy computes expiry as created_at + TTL, uploader trusts server time to compute backoff for retries
alex: looking at kms-proxy config from last deploy: GRANT_TTL=60 (seconds) but uploader retry backoff adds ~40-50s before final decrypt attempt
priya: so race: grant lives 60s, uploader tries to decrypt ~63-65s after grant creation occasionally -> InvalidGrant
morgan: mitigation options: (1) increase GRANT_TTL to 300-600s temporarily, (2) fix NTP on fleet, (3) add jitter/retry sooner. short-term I'd do (1) + (2)
sam: I can roll a hotfix to kms-proxy to bump GRANT_TTL to 600s and add a gauge metric grant_ttl_current so we detect if TTL <= 120 in future. low blast radius. canary first.
priya: please also add a policy alert: if Decrypt fails with InvalidGrant and time since CreateGrant > 30s, surface as 'possible clock skew / ttl misconfig'
alex: CloudTrail/CloudWatch logs show CreateGrant at 11:02:55, GenerateDataKeyWithGrant at 11:02:56 and Decrypt at 11:03:58 -> 63s gap. matches TTL 60s.
morgan: any config changes in last week that would reduce TTL? search in git: last commit to infra/kms-proxy config bumped down from 300->60 in commit 9f7b2c (author: infra-optimizer).
lee: ping infra-optimizer? not in thread. but we should revert that commit or at least explain rationale in PR
sam: deploying hotfix canary now -> ci/87654 (staging canary)
ops-bot: deploy canary started by sam: http://ci.internal/87654 :white_check_mark:
sam: canary healthy, increasing GRANT_TTL to 600s in staging. will monitor decrypt error rate and grant metrics for ~15m
alex: re-run restore-canary -> queued
alex: restore-canary finished successfully on attempt #2 after canary rollout :tada:
priya: next steps: (A) schedule fleet ntp check/fix (eng-sre) (B) revert the 9f7b2c change or add a rational in PR with telemetry (C) add audit alert for CreateGrant->Decrypt delta > TTL-10s (D) record postmortem note in encryptops runbook
morgan: i can own (C) and (D). sam owns (A) and (B) with eng-sre
sam: ack, creating tickets: ENGSEC-4321 (ntp sweep), INFRA-9876 (revert/better PR), SEC-4322 (alert rule)
lee: small follow-up: also check systemd-timesyncd vs ntpd differences on older AMIs, a couple uploader images had timesync disabled during image build
alex: thanks all. marking this thread resolved after tickets created and canary success.
ops-bot: incident closed by alex (restore-canary-failures) :white_check_mark:
